Synopsis:
    The Bank of Korea delivered a second consecutive 25bps rate hike to 3.00%, citing persistent inflation above target and financial stability risks including an overheating housing market. Governor Shin signaled a likely pause to assess impact before any further tightening, with the dot plot pointing to a probable terminal rate of 3.25% by end-2026. The BOK raised its 2026 growth forecast to 3.3% while leaving inflation unchanged at 2.7%. Markets expect a Q4 hold with one additional hike likely in Q1 2027. The move is framed within a divided global central bank environment, with the Fed holding restrictive and the BoJ cautious.
